title: The last two hours.
subject: PNN: Two hours left. Six houses. A study of why every deadline has a last-minute.
preheader: The Whities posted with two hours to spare. The Institute has a study on last minutes. It ends with a tote bag.

featuredCase.teaser: **The Tightie Whities announced they were 'back in the game' with two hours left in it.** Six teams. One warning that doubles as a receipt. A pink satin pair that looks awfully familiar, a lawn dressed as a white flag, and a door in costume. The Pyro Posse and the Crimson Crew have already replied. PNN has a rain-soaked composite sketch, a theory about the laundry, and one question: *why so late?* *The answer is in the case file. So is the spelling dispute.*
featuredCase.hook: including the sketch desk's rain-soaked composite and the Tighty versus Tightie spelling dispute

image.alt: A pencil-and-charcoal police sketch on aged paper headed PNN RECONSTRUCTION: THE LAST-MINUTE BRIEF. A faceless, hunched figure in a dripping white hoodie sprints through heavy rain toward a lit porch lantern, carrying a roll of white plastic sheeting and pink satin briefs under one arm, a phone reading 2:00:00, and a soggy plate of cookies. A broken umbrella lies behind them. Red string links pinned sketches of a rain cloud, a clock, pink briefs, a laundry basket, and notes reading why so late?, reused?, dissension?, napkin run?, and laundry day? A red stamp reads CUTTING IT CLOSE.
image.caption: PNN reconstruction: an AI-generated illustration of an alleged last-minute sweep, not a photograph.

tickerItems.text: Edition 011: a study finds 100% of deadlines are met in the last two hours, and one was met by a tote bag. The Whities own a tote bag.
Institute for Collaborative Mischief: 61 of 63 deadlines were met in the final two hours. One was met early. One is still negotiating.
Lost: one rain delay, slightly used. Last seen at the deadline. Finder asked to return it to the Tightie Whities, retroactively.

sections.kicker: SPECIAL REPORT / THE INSTITUTE FOR COLLABORATIVE MISCHIEF
sections.heading:
The last two hours.
(A study of what a team can do with a roll of plastic, a pair of briefs, and a deadline.)

runs.text: The
Institute for Collaborative Mischief
has spent
nineteen minutes
reviewing every deadline ever set,
and several that were extended after a team begged.
Its finding, in the Institute's own words:
'The last two hours are the only hours anyone actually uses.'
The study was prompted by
PNN-020
, in which the
Tightie Whities
hit
all six other teams
with
two hours
left before the prank deadline, then announced they were
'back in the game.'
Until then, they had barely played, and had been in the file as the team things happened to: dog walks (PNN-003), plates nobody took (PNN-007), a 'Not Tonight' in satin (PNN-012).
The Institute calls this
'a comeback with a very short runway.'
The methodology:
sixty-three deadlines, observed from a lawn chair.
Sixty-one were met in the final two hours. One was met early, by the Black Webb Bandits, at 12:48 a.m. (
PNN-019
), and then buried between two witch messages.
The sixty-third is still being negotiated.
The pattern is always the same.
A team says 'we have plenty of time.' It has plenty of time. It keeps having plenty of time right up to the minute it has none.
Then a tote bag appears. The Institute calls this
'the most reliable event in mischief: the sudden appearance of a tote bag.'
PNN is not saying the Whities
waited on purpose.
PNN is saying the notice on the porch comes from the
'Department of Team Performance,'
and the Department's own lead time was
two hours.
Rating: adequate dimensions. Inadequate notice.

sections.heading: The numbers, such as they are

items.text: **Time left on the deadline when the Whities posted.** *The Bandits posted 48 minutes into the last day (PNN-019). Between the two posts sits a fall festival, a great many napkins, and the Silver Bullets' bedtime.*

**Teams hit.** *The same count as the Pink Sweep (PNN-012 to 017). If it took one napkin run, forty-one minutes, that is under seven minutes a house. The Institute has asked for the footage. There is no footage. There is a lantern.*

**Spellings of the team's own name, in one night.** *'Tighty' in the message, 'Tightie' on the notice. PNN has not seen this much disagreement since the Pyro Posse spelled 'strategy' with an O (PNN-008).*
**Pair of pink satin briefs, possibly seen twice.** *Same satin and lace as 'Not Tonight' in PNN-012, new fine print. Return policy: unknown. Sender: not consulted.*
**Replies on file.** *One from the team that singed the Whities' laundry (PNN-005). One from a team that says briefs are sails. Both used exclamation points. One used four emojis.*
**Pink suspects caught.** *The pink house was hit too. Clueso has requested a more cooperative set of facts.*
**Chance a warning posted two hours before the deadline is also a receipt.** *The Institute has checked. It has also been checking the rain.*

runs.text: Lead finding:
a deadline is only a suggestion until the last two hours.
After that it is a lifestyle.

sections.heading:
The seven stages of a last-minute prank.
(Stage five may involve rain.)

runs.text: Stage 1 / The Calendar.
Someone looks at the date. The date looks back. 'Is the deadline tonight?' It has been tonight for some time.
The Bandits had already posted at 12:48 a.m. (PNN-019). Nobody remembers who saw it.
Stage 2 / The Vote.
The ranks split. One faction wants toilet paper. One wants plastic. The weather has no vote.
The Black Webb Bandits are said to have fought this exact battle a couple of nights ago, and the toilet paper won. PNN cannot confirm. PNN has chosen to enjoy it.
Stage 3 / The Laundry.
Inventory. Someone checks the basket. The basket is not ready. Someone else checks the dryer. The dryer is 'almost.'
The Institute does not elaborate on this stage, and neither will the Whities.
Stage 4 / The Satin.
A pink pair in the closet, with lace. 'Do we still have the...' Yes. They still have the... New fine print is added.
PNN-012 is not consulted.
Stage 5 / The Dash.
Rain, probably. A sheet of plastic, a handful of rocks, and a very good umbrella that does not survive.
Nothing is damaged, and everyone is a little damp. Rules 5 and 6 still apply, even at a run.
Stage 6 / The Post.
'Back in the game. Watch out for last-minute pranking.'
A warning, or a receipt. The Institute says both.
The message says 'Tighty.' The notice says 'Tightie.'
The ranks are still divided.
Stage 7 / The Replies.
The Pyro Posse found some lucky underwear. The Crimson Crew found some emergency sails.
Nobody found the witches. The witches are elusive, and as far as PNN can tell, unbribed (PNN-002).

sections.heading:
Two teams answered. Two rumors arrived.
(PNN answered the answers.)

runs.text: Pyro Posse.
'We were on you from the start!'
True: it started with a clothesline (PNN-005).
'Shouldn't have waited until the last minute.'
Advice on timing from the team that posted its own prank and deleted it before the victims got home.
Rating: four emojis out of four. Subtlety: pending.
Crimson Crew.
'Another spectacular top tier entertainment value observed from our looking glass!'
The Crew used nearly the same words after the pink team boarded its porch (PNN-014).
'These are the emergency sails for when we cruise to an easy victory!'
Rating: seaworthy, as long as nobody mentions PNN-010.
Open the file →
Rumor: the Bandits and the forecast.
PNN hears the Black Webb Bandits split over whether to toilet-paper their last round at all, since rain was coming. In the end, they papered every one.
Spiders love rain. Toilet paper does not.
No minority report has been filed.
Rumor: the baby shower nobody threw.
PNN hears some houses the pink team pranked were later approached by friends and neighbors with congratulations on a baby girl, apparently believing they had seen a gender reveal.
PNN has no word of any baby. PNN has every word of pink.
The pink team has not commented. It is, as always, wearing sunglasses.
Lead finding:
the only thing more convincing than a pink web is a pink web in good lighting.
LOST: One pink satin pair, slightly re-lettered.
Last seen in PNN-012, and apparently again. Finder asked to return it to the sender, with a receipt.
FOUND: One lucky pair of underwear, 'in poor condition.'
Owner may claim it from the Pyro Posse, with identification and a very good explanation.
WANTED: One rain delay.
Slightly used. For the Tightie Whities, retroactively.
FOR SALE: Emergency sails.
Seaworthy, tight, and white. Crimson Crew pre-owned. Buyer supplies own ship.
SERVICES: Spelling.
Tightie, with an 'ie.' References: the notice.
FOUND: One baby girl, reportedly.
Not found. Never lost. Neighbors are asked to stop congratulating.
NOTICE: The deadline has passed.
Scores are locked. Lurking is now voluntary.

sections.kicker: A NOTE FROM INSPECTOR CLUESO'S OFFICE
sections.heading:
Stand down.
(The deadline has passed. I have not stopped looking.)

runs.text: Inspector Clueso confirms the prank and photo deadline has passed and the scores are locked. He has
stood down tonight's stakeout.
No one needs to watch a porch for points tonight. He watched one anyway, from the car, with napkins.
The Whities hit all six teams,
the pink house included.
He wants it noted that
no pink suspects were caught.
A hit on a house is not a hit on a team. The pink team remains wanted everywhere, and caught nowhere.
Tomorrow is the scavenger hunt and the party.
Clueso will attend 'in an advisory capacity.' He has been told the party has no advisory capacity.
He would like all teams to bring snacks and alibis, and to leave the toilet paper at home.
He is bringing napkins.
Seen something?
Send game-related sightings and approved evidence to the
PNN Tip Line
His theory could use some facts.
Keep it friendly. Keep it to the game. No private details.
Reminder:
the prank and photo deadline has passed, and there are no points left to earn. Tomorrow's party is for fun:
be clever and fun, but don't be mean.
Nothing damaged (rule 5), no one's child targeted or frightened (rule 6), no one woken on purpose (rule 7), and nothing shared with outside groups (rule 8).
If any plastic or toilet paper is still on a lawn, please help the neighbors clean it up.
